content.text: Nap (short for Napoleon) is a classic English trick-taking game that gained massive popularity in Britain during the 19th and early 20th centuries. It is a quick, high-stakes game where players bid on how many of their five cards they can win in a trick-based battle against everyone else. It is known for its escalating bidding tiers named after Napoleonic battles (Wellington, BlÃ¼cher) and its simple yet ruthless scoring system.

Napoleon is a classic English pub game first documented in H.E. Heather's October 1875 edition of The Bazaar. It quickly became England's national five-card game, displacing Loo. The expression 'going Nap' (meaning to risk all on one attempt) derives from this game.
3-8 players; 4-5 is optimal. No permanent partnerships.
Standard 52-card pack. Cards rank A-K-Q-J-10-9-8-7-6-5-4-3-2. Often reduced based on player count.
Standard deck, poker chips or counters for stakes.
